title: Client Companies (Slots)
markdown:
The **clients** module (`openexecutive.clients`) adds **multi-client mode** for fractional executives: one Open Executive instance serving several client companies, exactly **one active at a time**. It generalizes the fixture switcher's swap machinery into named, durable *slots* — save files of the full company context. Single-company installs are untouched: nothing changes until a slot is explicitly created, and the `/clients` page shows only an intro until then.

## What a slot contains

Each slot lives at `company/_client_slots/<slug>/` (gitignored — client data is never committable):

| Artifact | What it carries |
| --- | --- |
| `state.db` | A transactionally-consistent copy of the shared SQLite DB — chat history, scheduled actions, departments, people, watchlist, audit/run history |
| `profile.yaml` | The company profile |
| `docs/`, `skills/` | Company documents (all file types) and company-authored skills — including customizations of built-ins `.hidden.yaml` (the company's hidden built-ins) |
| `mcp_servers.json` | Per-client external MCP tools (e.g. one client's Crayon or Google Workspace credentials) |
| `meta.json` | Display name + created/saved timestamps |

## Switching

`POST /clients/{slug}/activate` saves the current client back to its slot (`VACUUM INTO` for the DB copy), then restores the target: the DB through sqlite3's online **backup API** (the live file's inode never changes, so handles held elsewhere stay valid), the company artifacts by replacement, and the ChromaDB `company_docs` collection + company skills re-indexed from the restored directories (per-company `recent_research` chunks — research runs and indexed artifacts — are cleared, never carried across), with the built-in skill rows reconciled against the restored client's hidden and customized set. The isolated per-company collections are wiped in the same pass — `recent_research`, `notion_wiki`, `drive_docs`, and `inbound_attachments` (attachments are dropped and recreated rather than re-indexed: they have no source directory to rebuild from, and a row surviving a slot switch would be one client's attachment visible to the next). Idempotent schema initializers re-run after every restore, so a slot saved before a schema-adding deploy gains the new tables. The one-shot data sweeps the live DB gets at boot run there too (`app_migrations` keeps each to once per DB), among them cutting saved chat-app streams into conversations (`memory.conversations.split_existing_streams`). Activating a **blank** slot (created with `source: "blank"`, no `state.db` yet) empties every company table with the same sweep as the factory reset and fixture load (`memory.company_tables.wipe_per_company_tables`, below: every table but the company-independent ones, so a table added later is wiped too; the outgoing company's workflows are in its slot or the user's snapshot, so a blank client starts with none). That includes `email_thread_replies` (what the Executive mailed back, looked up by the recipient's address, so an advisor who writes for both clients would otherwise be shown the previous client's replies) and every standing fact, decisions included (`facts`, `facts_meta`) and re-seeds defaults — departments, principal briefs, cadences — so the new client's Today page works without a restart. That wipe covers the **derived caches** — `briefing_narrative` and `person_insights` — as well as authored state. They are regenerable, but `/today` serves them from cache and only regenerates in a background task, so a surviving row renders the *outgoing* client's briefing text under the incoming one, and `person_insights` reaches Discord, the MCP server, and the morning/end-of-day digests as well as the UI. Switching into a slot that already has `state.db` was never exposed: the sqlite backup API truncates the destination to an exact copy of the source.

After the restore, `fixture_loader.forget_company_caches()` drops the in-memory agent overrides, departments and people, so the next read sees the restored client. A factory reset and a fixture load or unload call the same function.

Every activation or create-from-current from single-company mode snapshots the original company to `_user_backup` first (the same restore point the fixture switcher uses), including `state.db`, a copy of the whole database; `POST /fixtures/unload` brings it back, every table included, and exits client mode.

## Invariants

- At most one slot is active — recorded in an allowlist-validated `.active_client` sentinel.
- **Only the active client is live**: its scheduled actions fire, its docs are indexed; parked clients sleep. The single-instance scheduler constraint is unchanged.
- Slot operations share the fixture switcher's destructive-op lock, so fixture loads, snapshots, resets, and slot switches serialize against each other. The Notion, Drive, OneDrive and Confluence sync ticks coordinate with the same lock without queueing on it: each skips its tick while the lock is held, fetches from its source unlocked, and takes the lock only for its short local write phase — aborting without writing if the active client changed mid-fetch (in-process only; a CLI run is a separate process the lock cannot see). A fixture and a client are never active simultaneously (slot ops refuse with 409 while a fixture is loaded); loading a fixture saves an active client back to its slot first, so demos can never destroy client work. Factory reset clears the active-client sentinel but preserves slot directories.
- `generated_fixtures` (the demo library) and `executive_control` (the operator pause switch) are operator-level and preserved verbatim across switches; activating a client never un-pauses the Executive.
- `workspace_settings` (solo/team mode, the user's time zone and the principal's role) is per company, not operator-level: a saved slot carries its own row in `state.db` (a slot saved before the role columns existed gets them on restore, with the role unset), and a blank slot's factory wipe returns it to the defaults (team, no zone, no role) before its briefs and cadences are seeded — so a new client never inherits the previous one's mode or brief times.
- **Every path that swaps the live company wipes from one registry**, `memory.company_tables`: blank/seed slot activation, factory reset, and fixture load. Three hand-maintained table lists is what let a leak survive in one path after being fixed in another (fixture load kept `department_notes`, so a shared department slug served the previous company's notes). `wipe_per_company_tables` reads the tables from `sqlite_master` and empties every one except `COMPANY_INDEPENDENT_TABLES`, the path's `keep` set, SQLite's own `sqlite_*` tables and full-text-search shadow tables, so a table that ships unclassified is wiped, the safe default. Every table the code creates is in `PER_COMPANY_TABLES` or in `COMPANY_INDEPENDENT_TABLES` with its reason (the fixture library, the pause switch, the eval scenarios, `install_owner`, and one-shot migration markers such as `departments_meta`, `dynamic_workflows_meta` and `delegation_upgrades`, which emptied would run again over the next company's data), and a unit test scans every `CREATE TABLE` and fails on a table in neither — a new table needs a decision there, not an edit to each path. A path leaves a per-company table in place only through a named exception with its reason: `KEPT_ON_EVERY_SWAP` (empty: the user's snapshot and each slot hold the whole database) and `KEPT_ON_FIXTURE_SWAP` (`dynamic_workflows`, `saved_tools` and `saved_tool_versions`, authored; `audit_log`, which load and unload keep by design; `workspace_settings`, which the fixture path sets itself from `workspace.yaml`; the knowledge review state, which belongs with knowledge files a fixture does not swap; and `outside_content_mode`, the owner's Safety level, whose missing row reads as Balanced). The wipe deletes children before parents from the database's own foreign keys and drops the in-process Agent Council override cache. A reset writes the principal's People row back afterwards and keeps `install_owner`. On the fixture path it runs in `_apply_state_from_source`, unconditionally and before the seeders: a fixture needs only `profile.yaml`, so gating it on `memory.json` would skip exactly the loads that still swap the company. It also runs before any file is swapped, so a failed wipe (a locked database) leaves the outgoing company whole. A load from the user's own company always snapshots it first, and a failed snapshot stops the load (`FixtureSnapshotError`) before anything is wiped; unload puts the whole saved database (`_user_backup/state.db`) back over the fixture's.
- **Progress updates are off while a slot or a demo fixture is live** (judged by whether its sentinel file exists, so an unreadable or damaged sentinel counts as live, as does a failed check). `PROGRESS_SOURCES` is process-wide, so an update from another agent would otherwise land in, and be sent to the founders of, whichever company is live. A submit waits up to 10 seconds for the destructive-op lock and is refused as unavailable only if a slot, fixture or sync operation still holds it then. A relay takes the lock only around its local steps, never across a chat send, and stops once its own row is no longer there and pending (every swap, a factory reset included, wipes or replaces the table) or a sentinel appears. Until sources can be bound to a slot, the feature is unavailable on a multi-client instance (see Integrations).
- Loading a fixture while no fixture is active asks for a typed `LOAD` first, as Reset everything asks for `RESET`; a load over another fixture does not ask.
- Do **not** treat `person_insights`' `input_hash` as a guard against this. It covers per-person signals (role, principal flag, status, counters, availability, authority and department scope, bucketed timestamps, the UTC day) but carries no person, name or company identity, and the cache key is `person_id` — a reused autoincrement PK. An outgoing principal and a freshly seeded incoming one hash identically whenever those signals coincide, which is ordinary steady state for a seeded slot.
- Each client gets a stable Honcho workspace (`openexec-client-<slug>`) so peer memory survives parking; fixture teardown paths recognise the prefix and never delete these.

## Caveats

`mcp_servers.json` is read by the MCP gateway at process startup — a switch that changes it takes effect on the next API restart (the activate response carries `mcp_config_changed`). Scheduled actions whose `run_at` passed while a client was parked are claimed on the first tick after activation; authority gates still apply, but expect the returning client's overdue follow-ups to fire shortly after a switch.

Two residuals. `/today`'s background regeneration tasks capture the outgoing company's data and can write it back into the live DB for up to roughly 25 seconds after the wipe — on **every** swapping path, fixture load/unload and slot activation alike, since those writers neither take the destructive-op lock nor check company identity. For `person_insights` it does not self-heal: the late write stores the outgoing `input_hash`, which the incoming person's signals often match, so the stale note survives until the UTC-day bucket rolls. Closing this needs company identity in the cache hash or those writers taking the lock. Second, `eval_scenarios` is kept across every switch and unload (`_GLOBAL_TABLES`) and by every wipe (`COMPANY_INDEPENDENT_TABLES`): the scenarios people wrote belong to the instance, not a client.

## Setting up a new engagement with AI

`POST /clients/generate` turns **real intake material** into a reviewable draft of the client: profile, org, roster, starter docs, and known history. Intake material is pasted text (kickoff-call notes, a brief, website copy) and/or **file attachments** (PDF, Word, Excel, CSV, Markdown/text; the request is multipart). Each attachment's extracted text both feeds the draft and is appended to the bundle as a `source_<name>.md` company doc, so it lands in the seed slot and is indexed into the `company_docs` collection on activation alongside the AI-written docs (extracted text, not the original binary; legacy `.xls` is unsupported). It runs the Council-configurable `engagement_intake` agent — the grounded sibling of the demo fixture generator (same bundle schema, validation, and repair-retry; the Company Simulator's fictional path is unchanged). Grounding rules: extract, don't invent — unstated numbers stay null, only people named in the material appear, docs are engagement working documents (intake brief, current-state summary, stakeholder map, open questions), and **no contact handles are ever imported**, even if present in the notes.

Saving the reviewed draft (`POST /clients` with `source: "generated"`) writes a **seed slot**: profile and docs as normal slot artifacts, plus `people.yaml` / `departments.yaml` / `memory.json` in the same shapes curated fixtures use. Nothing touches live state until activation, when the blank-restore path applies the seed files with the fixture loader's seeders, so the slot has exactly the departments the draft supplied. A blank slot, like a new install and the factory reset, starts with no departments. After the first save-back writes `state.db`, the seed files remain as the engagement's birth record but are no longer consulted; `meta.json` records `origin: "generated"` and the intake notes.

## The practice layer: engagement metadata + cockpit

Each slot's `meta.json` carries optional **engagement metadata** — your role for the client, engagement status (active/paused/winding down/completed), start and renewal dates, retainer (display only), and primary contact — editable via `PATCH /clients/{slug}` for active *and* parked slots, because meta.json lives outside the swapped client state. Renewal awareness deliberately lives here and never as scheduled actions (those swap with the client and would vanish when parked).

The **practice cockpit** (`GET /clients/cockpit`) gives cross-client awareness without touching the one-active-client ceiling: the active client is counted from the live DB, and each parked client's `state.db` is opened **read-only, in place** — no activation, no lock. Cards roll up pending/overdue follow-ups, awaiting replies, unread alerts, and renewal countdowns. Parked data is as fresh as the slot's last save point and every card says so; one broken slot degrades to a single error-flagged card, never a failed board. Cockpit cards link to the **engagement value report** — a workflow that turns the client's own record (decisions, deliverables, follow-through) into a renewal-ready artifact, reading parked clients without activating them. With two or more clients, `/today` gains an "Across your clients" section for the parked ones — single-company installs see none of this, anywhere.

## Overnight rotation (cockpit v2)

With `CLIENT_ROTATION_ENABLED=true` (off by default), a nightly scheduled job (`CLIENT_ROTATION_TIME`, default 03:30 UTC) activates each parked client in turn, generates its morning brief as an artifact in that client's own record, runs its monitor scan, saves it back, and **always restores the original active client** — then delivers one cross-client digest via the original client's principal channel. Two safety rails matter: the scheduler **pauses claiming** while the rotation's `.rotation_in_progress` marker exists (so a just-activated client's overdue outbound backlog can never fire at 3am — rotation does brief + monitors only, never outbound), and the rotation row is re-seeded after every slot activation because scheduled rows swap with the client. Completed engagements and never-activated slots sleep through rotation; per-client failures are skipped and reported in the digest.

## API + UI

`GET /clients` (list + active + fixture status), `POST /clients` (`source: "current"` captures the live company and activates; `"blank"` creates an empty client to onboard fresh; `"generated"` saves a reviewed intake draft as a seed slot), `POST /clients/generate` (grounded AI draft from intake notes and/or file attachments; multipart), `PATCH /clients/{slug}` (engagement metadata), `GET /clients/cockpit` (practice board), `POST /clients/save` (checkpoint without switching), `POST /clients/{slug}/activate`, `DELETE /clients/{slug}` (refuses the active slot). The `/clients` page lives under Settings → advanced tools.

**Knowledge review state per slot.** `_ensure_schemas` re-runs the idempotent schema inits after a restore, including `ReviewStore.initialize_db` followed by `sync_builtin_registrations`. Without that second call a freshly activated slot carried an empty `review_items` table until the next process restart; now it gets the shipped docs as trusted defaults straight away, matching a normal boot.

Attunement adds no per-client table of its own beyond the `attunement_usage` daily call counter and the `proactive_outcomes` ledger, both in the per-company registry every swap wipes: open loops live in `scheduled_actions` and message attribution / feedback in `chat_messages`, both already swapped with the slot. The engagement report's "follow-ups completed" count excludes open loops (`kind != 'open_loop'`): they are recorded `done` but are promises someone made, not follow-ups the Executive completed.

Always in the loop's tables (`history_notes`, `history_settings`, `history_person_settings`, `history_excluded`) are in the per-company registry, so neither a slot nor a demo inherits another engagement's notes.

Take the lead's tables (`take_the_lead.TABLES`: `take_the_lead`, `take_the_lead_rules`, `take_the_lead_log`) are per company the same way, in the per-company registry, so a slot starts with both switches off, no added rules and nothing in its log.

Act as me's tables (`delegation.schema.TABLES`: `delegation_settings`, `delegation_voice`, `delegation_voice_history`, `delegation_drafts`, `delegation_inbox_watch`, `delegation_inbox_messages`) are per company too, in the per-company registry through that one list, so a table added there is wiped by every company swap, and a blank client starts with it off, no writing profile and no inbox watcher. The inbox watcher never scans while a client slot is active. Each person's own-Gmail credential is a file outside the slot, re-checked against the live roster on every use, and "How I write" never keeps verbatim exemplars while a client slot is active, so one client's mail never lands in another client's state.

The People list's newer tables are per company as well: `person_emails` (email aliases) and the roster-request ledger (`roster_requests`, `roster_request_messages` — held messages from senders not yet on the roster — and `roster_ack_log`). They name who wrote to this company and its people's other addresses, so they are in the per-company registry (the wipe orders them before `people` from the foreign keys): a blank client or a loaded fixture starts with no aliases and nobody waiting. A saved slot carries them in `state.db` with the rest of the People data; the company's `company_domains` setting travels with its `workspace_settings` row the same way. The Telegram chats the bot has seen (`telegram_chats`, which the People and department pickers offer by name) name who wrote to it, so every company swap wipes them too.
